title: The v3 CSS Entry Point knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which principle is most useful when applying The v3 CSS Entry Point?
options: It makes every interface responsive and accessible without testing.
It runs all utility classes as JavaScript in the browser.
migration depends on the old version, new build integration and browser support requirements
It removes the need to understand HTML semantics, the CSS cascade or browser behavior.
questions.answer_key: migration depends on the old version, new build integration and browser support requirements
questions.explanation: The v3 CSS Entry Point is best understood through the syllabus topics: The @tailwind directives, Base, component, and utility layers, Preflight behavior. Choose the technique deliberately and verify the result.

questions.prompt: Which workflow is strongest when working with the v3 css entry point?
options: Skip narrow-screen testing because utility-first CSS is automatically responsive.
work in a branch, follow the official upgrade guide and compare representative pages
Add classes until a screenshot looks acceptable without inspecting generated CSS.
Assume that starting a development server proves every page and state works.
questions.answer_key: work in a branch, follow the official upgrade guide and compare representative pages
questions.explanation: A reliable workflow checks generated CSS and the actual interface. Related topics include: The @tailwind directives, Base, component, and utility layers, Preflight behavior, Custom CSS within v3 layers.

questions.prompt: Which common mistake should you avoid when applying the v3 css entry point?
options: do not mix v3 and v4 directives or configurations without a migration plan
Document intended behavior and test representative content.
Use the official documentation for version-specific behavior.
Check keyboard states where controls are involved.
questions.answer_key: do not mix v3 and v4 directives or configurations without a migration plan
questions.explanation: Good styling work is verified, version-aware and tested with realistic content and input methods.
